1.note: Lit. 'the Roman language'; de' Rossi may mean Latin or Italian (vernacular translations of Xenophon had appeared). The two works are the Cyropaedia and the Anabasis.

2.note: Cambyses, Mandane, Astyages, as in Cyropaedia 1.2.1.

3.note: Pontus Euxinus (Black Sea) and Cyprus, cf. Cyropaedia 8.6.21 and 8.8.1.

5.note: Tanaoxares, Cyrus' younger son in Cyropaedia 8.7.11.

6.note: Chapter 18 of Imrei Binah, per the author's reference.

8.he: ויהרוג את המלך אחיו וישב על כסאו בשלום ושקט
8.note: This contradicts Xenophon, in whose Anabasis Cyrus the Younger is killed at Cunaxa and Artaxerxes II continues to reign; de' Rossi's summary is mistaken or his text is corrupt.

9.note: Sense unclear; probably: the rabbinic tradition of only four Persian kings was not based on this verse, as stated earlier. 'The four writers' presumably refers to sources treated in chapters 31-34.
